page: Amazon Web Services x8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the 64-bit ARM architecture with AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier performance in memory-intensive operations. The instance achieves top-tier results in large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth, as well as in PassMark memory scores and database operations. Geekbench multi-core performance and software compilation with Clang also rank in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and text processing are strong, while single-core CPU benchmarks generally fall into the average category.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier memory bandwidth make this instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, and software compilation. However, tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators, which limits its utility for local-storage-heavy tasks or GPU-dependent workloads. Additionally, text generation for small LLM models is weak, though medium-model text generation remains strong.
